feeConfigTreasuries.note: FIXED. FeeConfig originally stored the treasury *owner* wallets below, but release_escrow/execute_dispute_outcome require each treasury to deserialize as a Token-2022 TokenAccount — and those wallet addresses did not exist on chain at all, so the entire release path was unexecutable on devnet. The escrow program gained an admin-gated `update_fee_config` (which takes the treasuries as mint-constrained token accounts, so a wallet can no longer be stored where a token account belongs), was upgraded in place, and FeeConfig now points at the settlement-mint ATAs recorded under feeConfigTreasuryAtas. Proven end to end on devnet: scripts/prove-devnet-escrow-release.ts ran a real create-vault -> deposit -> reserve -> create/fund escrow -> approve -> release cycle and asserted the exact 15 bps fee reaching all four treasuries at the 40/30/20/10 split (release signature 5o7Qk11e4yniEzrT8CesCZCCDQf5aVjt1DHCSqNcFqgwZkEz4gp2T1sQNTrnDZTdTSQezt5on3V1f1TUJEqs5tsF). The ATAs are for the devnet settlement (USDC) mint, NOT the OPEN mint: the settlement fee is a slice of the traded amount and is moved by transfer_checked out of the trade's own escrow vault, so treasuries must hold the mint trades settle in. One FeeConfig carries one treasury set, so fee collection currently supports a single settlement mint; a second traded stablecoin needs per-mint treasuries.

stakingAuthorities.note: Corrected by the staking program's new admin-only `update_staking_config`, applied on devnet in 2epNWu1sWqugMLRHwEvof6foAKzR1QZYD5CYeqg8Rxga45upPwcZjGDzRCg2nrkSL16jX7hAkGRNgyoP2e2gRtQK. ONE field was broken, not two. `slash_destination` held HLEB5akyStXEZfsTtgpnzexC4gyvDS5QNiYm1vDSHX4p, an address with NO ACCOUNT AT ALL on devnet, while `slash` requires that key to deserialize as a Token-2022 TokenAccount — so every slash failed at account load and the whole disincentive half of the arbitration incentive was dead code. Nothing rejected the value at write time because `initialize_staking_config` takes it as a plain Pubkey, the same class of defect that made release_escrow unexecutable until update_fee_config fixed it. The new instruction takes the destination as a mint-constrained token account, so neither a wallet nor a nonexistent address can be stored there again, and it rejects a zero authority.
stakingAuthorities.slashDestinationRationale: The emergency reserve owner's Token-2022 ATA for the OPEN mint. OPEN, not USDC: slashed tokens leave the stake vault, which is OPEN-denominated (verified on-chain), so a USDC fee treasury would fail on a mint mismatch. The emergency reserve rather than development or ecosystem because slashed stake is a forfeiture, not earned revenue — routing penalties into an operational budget would give the protocol a budgetary interest in slashing its own participants. [PROPOSED — NEEDS SIGN-OFF] Routing forfeitures to the arbitration pool instead, so honest arbitrators are paid by dishonest ones, is arguably better aligned but is a design change: the pool is a per-case PDA funded by merchant deposits, with no single global account to route to.
stakingAuthorities.rewardsAuthorityNote: EA8TyQ58... — unchanged by this update, and already correct. It does concentrate reward distribution on a single EOA, the same centralisation point crates/rewards documents for the cranker, recorded here so it is a known property rather than a later discovery. Governance-controlled distribution is the eventual answer and is deliberately not this change. Note the program takes both authorities as plain Pubkeys rather than requiring them to sign: a signature would prove at write time that somebody holds the key, but a PDA cannot sign a client transaction, and that rule would foreclose ever handing either authority to a program.

misconductCodes.note: [PROPOSED — NEEDS SIGN-OFF] OFS-4100 §4 enumerates the slashing triggers but assigns them no codes. 1 = revealed vote outside dispute consensus (OFS-2400 §328), emitted by the relay in crates/slashing.

governanceForfeitDestination.note: FIXED. GovernanceConfig.forfeit_destination held VueuQemTWZcZXMhfN1jRH1vs1zeWXYvzhDPC8uxJARF — the ecosystem treasury *owner* wallet, not a token account. This is the same class of defect as the FeeConfig treasuries and staking's slash_destination: initialize_governance_config takes the field as a plain Pubkey, so nothing rejected a wallet at write time. The impact was wider than the field's name suggests. refund_or_forfeit_deposit loads forfeit_destination as a Token-2022 TokenAccount in its *account context*, before the handler chooses a branch, so account loading failed on every call — REFUNDS TOO, not just forfeitures. A proposal's deposit could never be settled either way, in either direction. The governance program gained an admin-gated `update_governance_config` which takes the destination as a mint-constrained token account (and additionally requires governance_config.mint == mint, since GovernanceConfig records its own mint), so neither a wallet nor a wrong-mint account can be stored there again.
governanceForfeitDestination.forfeitDestinationRationale: [PROPOSED — NEEDS SIGN-OFF] The ecosystem treasury owner's Token-2022 ATA for the OPEN mint. OPEN, not USDC: the governance deposit vault is OPEN-denominated, so a USDC treasury would fail on a mint mismatch. The owner is deliberately unchanged from the wallet the config already named — the stored value recorded where forfeited deposits were meant to go, so this corrects the type error without quietly relocating protocol income. CONSIDERED AND DECIDED THE OTHER WAY: slashDestination above routes forfeitures to the emergency reserve on the reasoning that penalties should not fund an operational budget, or the protocol acquires a budgetary interest in punishing its own participants. A forfeited proposal deposit is arguably the same class of forfeiture and the same argument applies. It was weighed and decided for the ecosystem treasury for now, on the grounds that deposit forfeiture is triggered by a token-weighted vote missing quorum rather than by an authority with a budget, which weakens (but does not eliminate) the incentive concern. Recorded here so the argument does not have to be rediscovered.

governanceForfeitDestination.decodeDiscipline: OFS-4200 §7.1. The script decodes GovernanceConfig with a single moving cursor and asserts the walk consumes exactly the account length minus its two trailing u8 bumps (138 of 140 bytes). This is not ceremony: an earlier StakingConfig decode in this repo used independently-computed per-field offsets, skipped a 32-byte field, and reported two adjacent pubkeys with their identities transposed — both well-formed, both wrong, and it read as correct until the chain contradicted it. A cursor that must balance cannot skip a field silently. The decoded values are also individually recognisable (5001 bps, 5000 OPEN at 9 decimals, 604800s), which catches a transposition that a balanced walk alone would not.
governanceForfeitDestination.depositVaultBalanceAtFix: 0 — no deposit had ever been taken, so the correction is forward-looking and there was no stranded balance to migrate.

devnet_programs.note: Deployed via `solana program deploy --url devnet` and initialized via a one-off script using the new Rust SDK's onchain::{escrow,staking,governance} builders (Phase 8's own deploy+init step, pulled forward from Phase 9's original schedule — Phase 8's app wiring needs a real devnet deployment to cut over against). FeeConfig/StakingConfig/GovernanceConfig singletons are all live: staking_config.mint = governance_config.mint = the real devnet OPEN mint above (decimals 9); staking's unbonding/slash_bps and governance's quorum/threshold/deposit/vote_lock all use OFS-4100's own recommended [PROPOSED — NEEDS SIGN-OFF] figures, not invented values. LAYOUT CHANGE: StakingConfig's flat min_stake plus special-cased min_stake_arbitrator were replaced by a per-role min_stake_by_role array ([u64; 7], indexed by Role), and the minimums are now actually enforced by `stake` and `request_unstake` — previously they were stored and read by nothing, so any amount was accepted. The already-deployed config account was rewritten in place by the program's own `migrate_staking_config` instruction (scripts/migrate-devnet-staking-config.ts) rather than being recreated, so the config PDA and both token vaults kept their addresses. Live values: 1,000 OPEN for every role except Arbitrator at 10,000 (both per OFS-4100 §4) and NotificationProvider at 5,000 (protocol-steward decision; OFS-4100 §4 amended to record it).

disputeParameters.note: Dispute-case parameters introduced with the arbitration security fix. All three are [PROPOSED — NEEDS SIGN-OFF]: they are economic/liveness choices, not values any spec fixes. commitDisputeVote is now gated on the committer holding the Arbitrator role's minimum stake (min_stake_by_role[Arbitrator], currently 10,000 OPEN) — previously any wallet could commit, and since initialize_stake_account is permissionless and a zero balance is legal, seven throwaway wallets could occupy all MAX_ARBITRATORS seats for the price of rent, reveal zero-weight votes, and drive the tally to an all-zero tie that resolved to InvalidDispute, returning the escrow to the seller. A merchant could keep a buyer's money after the buyer had sent fiat. The tally now also skips zero-weight reveals, and an undecided round no longer pays anyone: it re-opens the case, bounded by maxDisputeRounds, after which the escrow splits evenly so neither side profits from forcing indecision. MutualSettlement likewise splits evenly rather than falling into the merchant-wins arm as it previously did; a ratio-bearing partial settlement (OFS-2400 §17) remains future work. minDisputeWindowSecs is deliberately low — it is a liveness guard against a same-block window, not the anti-squatting defence, which is the stake gate; a production floor should reflect real arbitrator discovery latency over gossip.
disputeParameters.undecidedRoundPolicy: re-open the case; split the escrow evenly once maxDisputeRounds is reached
disputeParameters.settlementFeeOnEvenSplit: none — the protocol did not successfully arbitrate

rewardsAndFees.note: OFS-4100 §9 implementation. Three fees with three payers, each now with an identified source of funds: the BUYER bears the settlement fee (deducted from the escrowed amount at release, in the traded stablecoin); the MERCHANT bears the ad-listing fee (charge_ad_listing_fee, debited from their OPEN liquidity vault) and the arbitration deposit (open_dispute_case, also from their OPEN vault, whoever opened the case). Before this, ad_listing_fee and dispute_filing_fee were stored on FeeConfig and read by no instruction, and no instruction funded the staking rewards vault, so no reward was ever payable.
rewardsAndFees.settlementFeeBpsStatus: [DECISION — protocol steward] 0.85%, superseding the 15 bps originally deployed. Governance-updatable via update_fee_config.
rewardsAndFees.arbitrationPoolNote: Singleton OPEN token account owned by the FeeConfig PDA, created by initialize_arbitration_pool. Deliberately NOT one of the four settlement-fee treasuries: those are external wallet-owned accounts routing revenue, whereas this holds funds still owed either back to a merchant or forward to arbitrators. Mixing a liability with revenue would make neither auditable.
proposedNeedsSignOff: Arbitration deposit disposition when the merchant WINS or the outcome is InvalidDispute: returned to the merchant's OPEN vault. The steward specified forfeiture only for 'merchant loses'; 'deposit' ordinarily implies return when not at fault, but this was not stated.

Arbitration deposit disposition at the MAX_DISPUTE_ROUNDS terminal even split (no consensus, no loser): returned to the merchant's OPEN vault. Forfeiting on 'nobody reached consensus' would punish a merchant for an outcome the arbitrators failed to produce.
Arbitration deposit disposition on MutualSettlement: returned, same reasoning — neither side was found at fault.

Partial/zero deposit collection when the merchant's OPEN vault cannot cover the fee: the case opens anyway with whatever was available, and the shortfall is recorded in the ArbitrationDepositTaken event. Requiring the full deposit would let a merchant make themselves undisputable by keeping their OPEN vault empty, which is a far worse failure than one case's arbitrators going unpaid.
Ad-listing fee destination: the development treasury. OFS-4100 §6 sets the fee's amount but names no destination, and splitting a small flat charge four ways would add four accounts to every listing.

Ad-listing fee charged via a dedicated instruction rather than at vault creation, deposit, or reservation: a merchant funds once but lists many times, and charging at reservation would bill per trade, which is the settlement fee's job.
rewardsAndFees.slashBelowMinimumNote: slash may now leave a balance below the role minimum, and deliberately does. Sweeping the remainder to zero would also restore the 'non-zero stake is a qualifying stake' invariant, but it turns a slash_bps penalty into total forfeiture for anyone staked at the minimum — the common case for arbitrators, and contrary to OFS-2400 §16's 'partial, moderate stake slash'. The invariant is instead enforced in StakeAccount::effective_stake, which returns 0 below the minimum, so governance vote weight and the dispute tally both ignore such an account while it keeps its tokens.
rewardsAndFees.eventsNote: The programs workspace previously contained zero emit!/#[event]. Reward, claim, slash, vault-funding, escrow-release (with the full four-way fee split), dispute-resolution, deposit-taken and reward-claim events are now emitted so an indexer can rebuild history from logs alone (OFS-4100 §9.4).
